questions.q: What does the SET clause in an UPDATE statement do?
options: Lists which table the UPDATE targets
Creates a new column on the table
Filters which rows will be changed
Lists one or more column = value assignments to apply to the matched rows
questions.explain: SET is where you specify exactly which columns change and what they change to.

questions.q: In 'UPDATE dbo.LessonDemo SET ListPrice = ListPrice * 1.10 WHERE Color = 'Red';', where does the multiplier apply?
options: Only to the first matching row
To a single shared average ListPrice across all red rows
To each matching row's own current ListPrice, computed per row
To every row in the table regardless of color
questions.explain: SQL Server reads each matching row's own current value and computes the new value from it -- every red row is updated from its own starting price.

questions.q: What happens if you run 'UPDATE dbo.LessonDemo SET Color = 'Discontinued';' with no WHERE clause?
options: Only the first row in the table is changed
Every row currently in the table has Color set to 'Discontinued'
SQL Server raises a syntax error because WHERE is required
No rows change until a WHERE clause is added
questions.explain: Just like a SELECT with no WHERE returns every row, an UPDATE with no WHERE applies its SET assignments to every row in the table.

questions.q: How many columns can a single SET clause update in one UPDATE statement?
options: As many as needed, separated by commas, as long as they belong to the table being updated
Two columns maximum
Only columns that are NOT NULL
Exactly one column per UPDATE statement
questions.explain: Multiple column = value assignments can be comma-separated in the same SET clause, all applied to the same matched rows.

questions.q: Why is it good practice to run the equivalent SELECT with the same WHERE clause before running an UPDATE?
options: It confirms exactly which rows will be changed before you commit to changing them
SQL Server requires a prior SELECT before any UPDATE
It automatically creates a backup of the affected rows
It is required to compute SCOPE_IDENTITY() afterward
questions.explain: Since UPDATE doesn't display the rows it changes, previewing with a matching SELECT catches a WHERE clause that's broader or narrower than intended.
